units.text: INT. EARNEST - CONTINUOUS
Morning-room in Algernon’s flat in Half-Moon Street.
The room is luxuriously and artistically furnished.
The sound of a piano is heard in the adjoining room.
Lane is arranging afternoon tea on the table, and after the music has ceased, Algernon enters.
Did you hear what I was playing, Lane?
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: I didn’t think it polite to listen, sir.
units.name: LANE

units.text: I’m sorry for that, for your sake. I don’t play accurately—any one can play accurately—but I play with wonderful expression. As far as the piano is concerned, sentiment is my forte. I keep science for Life.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: Yes, sir.
units.name: LANE

units.text: And, speaking of the science of Life, have you got the cucumber sandwiches cut for Lady Bracknell?
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: Yes, sir.
units.name: LANE

units.text: Hands them on a salver.
Inspects them, takes two, and sits down on the sofa.
Oh! . . . by the way, Lane, I see from your book that on Thursday night, when Lord Shoreman and Mr. Worthing were dining with me, eight bottles of champagne are entered as having been consumed.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: Yes, sir; eight bottles and a pint.
units.name: LANE

units.text: Why is it that at a bachelor’s establishment the servants invariably drink the champagne? I ask merely for information.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: I attribute it to the superior quality of the wine, sir. I have often observed that in married households the champagne is rarely of a first-rate brand.
units.name: LANE

units.text: Good heavens! Is marriage so demoralising as that?
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: I believe it is a very pleasant state, sir. I have had very little experience of it myself up to the present. I have only been married once. That was in consequence of a misunderstanding between myself and a young person.
units.name: LANE

units.text: Languidly .
I don’t know that I am much interested in your family life, Lane.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: No, sir; it is not a very interesting subject. I never think of it myself.
units.name: LANE

units.text: Very natural, I am sure. That will do, Lane, thank you.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: Thank you, sir.
units.name: LANE

units.text: Lane goes out.

Lane’s views on marriage seem somewhat lax. Really, if the lower orders don’t set us a good example, what on earth is the use of them? They seem, as a class, to have absolutely no sense of moral responsibility.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: Enter Lane.
Mr. Ernest Worthing.
units.name: LANE

units.text: Enter Jack.
Lane goes out .
How are you, my dear Ernest? What brings you up to town?
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: Oh, pleasure, pleasure! What else should bring one anywhere? Eating as usual, I see, Algy!
units.name: JACK

units.text: Stiffly .
I believe it is customary in good society to take some slight refreshment at five o’clock. Where have you been since last Thursday?
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: Sitting down on the sofa.
In the country.
units.name: JACK

units.text: What on earth do you do there?
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: Pulling off his gloves .
When one is in town one amuses oneself. When one is in the country one amuses other people. It is excessively boring.
units.name: JACK

units.text: And who are the people you amuse?
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: Airily .
Oh, neighbours, neighbours.
units.name: JACK

units.text: Got nice neighbours in your part of Shropshire?
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: Perfectly horrid! Never speak to one of them.
units.name: JACK

units.text: How immensely you must amuse them!
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: Goes over and takes sandwich.
By the way, Shropshire is your county, is it not?
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: Eh? Shropshire? Yes, of course. Hallo! Why all these cups? Why cucumber sandwiches? Why such reckless extravagance in one so young? Who is coming to tea?
units.name: JACK
